newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Three population experts receive U.N. award.
newsitem.headline: Three population experts receive U.N. award.

text.p: A Thai senator and birth control pioneer urged governments on Tuesday to review strict abortion laws that he said unintentionally caused the death of tens of thousands of women.

Senator Mechai Viravaidya was addressing a U.N. ceremony at which he and two other family planning experts were presented with the 1997 U.N. Population Award, consisting of diplomas, gold medals and an equal share of the monetary prize of $25,000. The winners' names were announced in February.

The other laureates were El Salvador's first lady, Elizabeth Aguirre Calderon Sol, director of her country's National Family Secretariat, and Professor Toshio Kuroda, director emeritus of Nihon University Population Research Institute.

Viravaidya, chairman of Thailand's Population and Community Development Association, said: "I respectfully urge all governments to review their restrictive laws which unintentionally sentence to death 70,000 women a year by denying them access to safe termination of their pregnancies."

He added: "In the midst of uncertainty of interpreting the law, it is men who legislate, harass and arrest, and it is the women who suffer. Our laws deny safe termination of pregnancy to the women who need it most desperately. We must stop this hypocrisy."
The U.N. Population Award is presented annually to individuals and institutions that have made outstanding contributions to increasing awareness of population problems and their solutions.

Taking part in Tuesday's ceremony were U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan, the executive director of the U.N. Population Fund, Dr. Nafis Sadik, and the chairman of the Population Award committee, ambassador Julio Armando Martini Herrera of Guatemala.
